# TERMs with `line` `formal-apparatus`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Formal apparatus** — results that hold whatever any substantive line concludes — gluing and contextuality, comparison of experiments and probes, identifiability, conservation, and thresholds for naming a unit; held as a second line by the general results other lines borrow, so that setting a substantive line aside does not retire them (ADR-040).

| [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md) v2 | sloppy, of a parametric model at a point and for an observation design: its Fisher information spectrum, in a declared chart, spreads over many decades with no gap that separates the parameter combinations that matter from those that do not; a graded property, distinct from ill-conditioning, from singularity and from a power-law spectrum | At the owner's suggestion of 2026-11-21, after the filing of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws": "a TERM for the mathematical (information geometric?) sense of 'sloppy' might be merited". The record used the word in that sense in several entries ([TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md), [TERM-137](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-137.md), [CLAIM-813](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-813.md), [CLAIM-820](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md), [CLAIM-812](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-812.md)) and in its readings of sloppy spectra ([THEORY-774](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-774.md), [THEORY-777](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-777.md)), without defining it. A model is sloppy, at a parameter point and for a given observation design, when the eigenvalues of its Fisher information, in a declared chart (conventionally the logarithms of its bare parameters), spread over many decades, and no gap among them marks off the combinations that matter from those that do not. The term separates this from four neighbours: ill-conditioning (one ratio, which a single gap can produce), singularity (a zero eigenvalue on a stratum), the hyperribbon (the chart-free shape of the predictions, [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md)), and a power-law spectrum (a sloppy spectrum falls by roughly a constant factor per rank, so it covers decades in proportion to the number of parameters). Its job is to let the record's entries on sloppiness, singular learning and effective dimension say which of these they mean. The source of the concept is Sethna and colleagues: LIT-2977, LIT-3009 and LIT-2994, read on 2026-11-21 (THEORY-2156, THEORY-2155, THEORY-2154), and LIT-2999, unread. They define sloppiness by example and by an eigenvalue spread "roughly evenly spaced" in log, and put its chart-free content in the widths of the model manifold; version 2 records what they say. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
